what:
From speed-sol2-link (speed of light, 'Debug lines' and 'The live runtime' in docs/v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-of-light.md).

1. dwarf.rs `sections(views, rows, files, size)`: the core (write.rs `Stage::debug`) now builds rows in parallel (DEBUG_CHUNK = 1024 functions per task, files numbered by first appearance, merged in order), so the serial encode is the remaining O(image) part of a Debug::Lines relink. Encode the line program per chunk of functions in parallel into per-chunk buffers sized first (row counts are known) and concatenate in order: byte-identical output to today's serial encode, with a differential test against the serial version kept under #[cfg(test)]. Leave the address sort fix-radix owns.
2. The design for O(change) debug lines (not needed for correctness): one CU and line program per chunk of functions with slack, so an edit re-encodes one chunk and the core rewrites only that range. Write it down in the doc if you do not build it.
3. Enabling for refused 00903: `build_hdr` lists FDEs outside .eh_frame only from `placed.functions`; to let native ELF FDEs (and their CIEs) move into Class::Patch it would have to list every FDE of the patch region's frame runs. Mach-O `__unwind_info` can name an FDE only by its offset in __eh_frame, so Mach-O patch FDEs can't leave __eh_frame without losing unwinding on relaunch. Say in the doc whether either is worth doing.

history.note: 1: dwarf.rs sections encodes subprograms, names and line sequences per 1,024 functions in parallel, joined by unwind::concat; same bytes and first error as the serial encode, kept as tests::sections_serial (test sections_in_pieces_are_the_serial_encodes_bytes); the address sort untouched. 2: the chunked-CU O(change) design is written in speed-of-light.md, 'The debug line program and subprograms', not built. 3: answered there: neither is worth doing (ELF: a second walk per patch for rare native changes; Mach-O: __unwind_info names an FDE only by its __eh_frame offset). Not yet built.
